item.title: Freezing temperatures and rain for Kerry as two weather warnings issued
item.description: Freezing temperatures and rain will hit Kerry overnight and tomorrow as two status yellow weather warnings have been issued for the county. Freezing temperatures are expected tonight, while heavy rain is expected tomorrow. The national forecaster is warning that both warnings could result in difficult travelling conditions. item.title: Over 21.5m containers returned in Kerry as part of Deposit Return Scheme
item.description: Today marks the second anniversary of the Deposit Return Scheme in Ireland. In Kerry, SuperValu and Centra say they have received over 21,566,077 for web container returns over the past two years. The two supermarket chains are part of the Musgrave Group, which has the largest number of Deposit Return Scheme locations. Advertisement Across Ireland, Musgrave is among the first retailers to reach 500 million container returns.

item.title: Tudor to become Tottenham interim head coach
item.description: Former Juventus boss Igor Tudor has agreed to become Tottenham's interim head coach until the end of the season. The Croatian will take over from the sacked Thomas Frank and be tasked with keeping them in the Premier League. Final details are still to be worked out but Tudor will take training on Monday. Advertisement Spurs will look to appoint a permanent manager in the summer.

item.title: Major injury blow for Ireland
item.description: And the Ireland men's cricketers have suffered a major injury blow ahead of tomorrow's T20 World Cup clash with Oman. Captain Paul Stirling suffered a knee ligament injury against Australia, and has been ruled out of the rest of the tournament. Ireland can still qualify for the last-eight, after Zimbabwe stunned the Aussies earlier today. Advertisement

item.title: Two state-supported Ukrainian accommodation centres in Kerry to return to original use
item.description: Two state-supported accommodation centres in Kerry are set to return to original use. The Department of Justice says the need for accommodation for people affected by the war in Ukraine is reducing. Nationally, at the beginning of 2026, 21,000 Ukrainians were living in 550 state-supported accommodation centres. Advertisement This is down from a peak of over 60,000 people fleeing the war living in such accommodation at one point. The state contract is ending in two accommodation centres in Kerry

item.title: Astellas’ expansion recognised as being among Europe’s top investment projects
item.description: Astellas’ expansion in Kerry and Dublin has been recognised as being among Europe’s top investment projects. Last year, the global pharmaceutical company announced it was to invest a further €129 million in its operations in this county and in the capital. The Japanese multinational is building a €330 million facility in Tralee and has a plant in Killorglin since the 1990s. item.title: Pereira to take over as Forest boss
item.description: It's understood Vitor Pereira has agreed a contract to take over as Nottingham Forest boss - and will sign on until the end of the season. The former Wolves head coach will replace Sean Dyche as the club's fourth permanent manager of the campaign. He was sacked this week with Forest just three points clear of the Premier League relegation zone. Advertisement

item.title: Keenan may be unavailable for entire Six Nations campaign
item.description: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has revealed that Hugo Keenan may be unavailable for the entire Six Nations campaign. The full-back was ruled out of last week's defeat to France with a hand injury picked up during their training camp in Portugal. Ireland continue their campaign with the visit of Italy to the Aviva Stadium tomorrow afternoon. Advertisement

item.title: Ukrainian athlete has appeal against disqualification from Winter Olympics dismissed
item.description: A Ukrainian athlete has had his appeal against disqualification from the Winter Olympics dismissed by the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Vladyslav Heraskavych was banned over his helmet, which featured pictures of his countrymen, killed by Russia. The International Olympic Committee ruled it broke its charter, which has been agreed by competitors. Advertisement But he's accused the governing body of being "on the wrong side of history".
